request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: If the Tenant, an occupant or a guest of the Tenant damages the unit on purpose or through carelessness, beyond normal wear and tear, the Tenant shall pay the reasonable cost of the repair.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
Yes, this clause is enforceable because it simply restates the statutory duty already placed on tenants by the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006*. Under the Act, a tenant is responsible for the repair of undue damage to the rental unit or residential complex that is caused wilfully or negligently by the tenant, another occupant of the rental unit, or a person whom the tenant permits in the residential complex.

Note that while the tenant's obligation to pay the reasonable cost of such repairs is legally enforceable, if there is a dispute over the fault or the cost, the landlord cannot unilaterally enforce payment and must apply to the Landlord and Tenant Board (under section 89) for an order determining the amount owed. 

Verdict: enforceable
Section: 34
